details: Forensics is an evidence-first Earth-system investigation prototype created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!”. The project helps users investigate what is changing, where it is changing, how much it is changing, and whether the available evidence supports a statistically significant trend. Users can select a location, environmental variable, and time range, then inspect data quality, annual observations, trend magnitude, statistical evidence, source metadata, spatial context, and limitations. The project uses NASA POWER monthly data for air temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. It applies a complete-calendar-year quality gate, parameter-specific aggregation, a 1991–2020 reference climatology, Theil–Sen trend estimation, and a modified Mann–Kendall method when the record is sufficient. Earth Forensics is designed to discourage overclaiming. It does not establish causation, official forecasting, daily event impact from monthly data, or automatic regional conclusions. Spatial results are exploratory context because nearby requests may share the same gridded source structure. The project was developed as a web application prototype using JavaScript/React-style frontend components and server-side application functions. The public repository contains the project documentation, methodology, presentation, and handoff materials. The complete Builder-generated source export is not currently included.
